blocks.text: You can integrate Google Cloud Platform (GCP) with Zscaler Deception to set up various GCP-specific decoy resources in your environment to lure adversaries. Depending on the type of decoy and its configuration, an adversary can access, interact, or perform malicious operations with the cloud decoys in different ways. Such activities are logged as attacks. You can view and analyze the attack details from the Deception dashboard.
Cloud Deception with GCP provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Configure decoys that mimic legitimate GCP resources, such as service accounts, cloud storages, cloud SQLs, secret managers, and artifact registries.
Lure internal and external adversaries to GCP decoy resources and proactively take remedial action.
Leverage landmine policies such as cloud lures, session lures, browser lures, and certain file decoys to lure internal adversaries.

blocks.text: You can deploy GCP decoys to detect malicious activities originating from adversaries within or outside your organization, depending on the type and configuration of the decoys. For example, lures for GCP decoys configured using landmine policies detect malicious activities from users within an organization, as the landmine policies are deployed in devices managed by your organization. On the other hand, GCP decoys with public visibility can detect malicious activities from external adversaries who enumerate them with various tools.

You can use Terraform-based deployment to set up the integration and deploy decoys in the GCP cloud. All necessary resources such as users, policies, etc. to manage Cloud Deception with GCP are deployed while setting up the integration. A health check lambda function is also deployed that monitors and updates the health status of the deployed decoys to the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal every 15 minutes.

Deception fetches only the logs associated with decoys from GCP using Logging query language. Deception deploys a logging bucket that is used to collect logs for public cloud storage decoys. For all other decoys, audit logs are used. The following permissions are used for the service account created during the integration:

blocks.item: LogViewer: Grants read-only access to view all standard logs, but excludes logs that might contain sensitive information.

privateLogViewer: Grants read-only access specifically to view private logs (e.g., Data Access audit logs) that are restricted from the standard LogViewer role. This is required to determine who accesses the decoys.
View access for _AllLogs view in the _Default logging bucket: This is required to retrieve all access logs associated with the decoys.

blocks.heading: About the Cloud Deception GCP Page

blocks.text: On the Cloud Deception - GCP page (Deceive > Cloud Deception > GCP), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Go to the GCP decoys listed as follows:
Service Account
Cloud Storage
Cloud SQL
Secret Manager
Artifact Registry
You can also check the status, edit, or delete your GCP decoys from the respective tabs. To learn more, see Managing GCP Decoys.
Configure the integration between GCP and Deception.
View the list of GCP projects added to the Deception Admin Portal. For each project, you can see:
Enabled: Indicates whether the logs for the GCP project are being polled.
Project ID: The project ID as configured in GCP.
Service Account Email: The email address of the service account created for accessing decoys and resources in GCP.
Logging Bucket: A cloud storage created for logging purposes.
Health Check Function URL: The URL of the health check function deployed to monitor and update the health status of the deployed decoys to the Deception Admin Portal.
Marked for Deletion: Indicates whether a GCP account was marked to be deleted from the Deception Admin Portal.
Manage Deception settings for a GCP account.
Download files for Terraform-based deployment.
Upload a Terraform state file.
